overall: Atlanta has experienced a dramatically suppressed day relative to the NWS-forecast high of 83°F. Cloud cover ranging from 62–100% through most of the morning and early afternoon, 0.74 inches of cumulative precipitation, and persistent northwest winds near 20 mph combined to cap heating. Temperatures actually dropped into the mid-60s during early afternoon before recovering back to match the early-morning maximum of 73.4°F by 17:19 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: ECMWF (74.2°F) and HRRR (73.5°F) are tightly aligned with observed conditions and credibly bracket the final TMAX near 73–74°F; NBM (79.5°F) is a clear outlier that failed to account for today's persistent cloud deck and precipitation. The NWS text forecast of 83°F overestimated today's high by roughly 9–10°F — the active cloud/precip regime invalidated the sunny-day assumption underlying that forecast.
max_temp_prediction: The daily maximum of 73.4°F was set around midnight/early morning and has not been exceeded despite a late-afternoon recovery. At 17:19 ET, the current temperature equals the running max, but with northwest winds near 20 mph, residual 62% cloud cover, and well past the typical peak heating window, meaningful further warming is unlikely. The final TMAX is expected to land near 73.5°F, with very low probability of exceeding 74–75°F; confidence is high given strong ECMWF/HRRR model agreement and the intraday model's 96.4% concentration in the 72–73°F bucket.
